title: Trail and Current
premise: Zephyrine Oyelaran, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries for a rescue that went wrong, survives on border-hopping river work until his old rival, Ines Kovač, hires his crew to run supplies up the Serein Gorge during monsoon season — the same route where his brother drowned and where he swore never to return. Mid-river, he discovers Ines's cargo is evidence that could clear his name but destroy the village downstream that sheltered him, forcing a choice between the truth that would restore his life and the loyalty that gives it meaning. When the boat begins leaking under the storm's assault, Zephyrine must rely on Amara, a stranger with her own buried past, to reach the gorge's head before the flood. He chooses truth over vindication, burning the evidence to save the village, and in doing so finally stops running — finding that memory, faced honestly, costs less than flight.
about_author: Hazel Okonkwo is a former river expedition cook who turned her seasons on West African and Alpine waterways into fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who can't go home, and lives wherever the ferry last dropped her.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. On the run in a border town, Zephyrine takes a risky cargo job to pay off a forged permit, revealing through flashbacks the rescue gone wrong that got him blacklisted. The beat is restless survival — a man who measures safety in miles already traveled.

chapters.title: Ines at the Dock
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. His old rival Ines Kovač appears with a contract: run supplies up the Serein Gorge before the monsoon peaks. Zephyrine refuses; she mentions his brother's name, and the refusal cracks. The beat is old wounds reopened by ambition dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Amara. A drifter with forged papers, Amara joins the crew and watches Zephyrine drill them ruthlessly on the boat, the Vela. She senses he's more afraid of the destination than the journey. The beat is wary curiosity hardening into reluctant respect.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Water
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The crew enters the Serein Gorge; landmarks trigger memories of his brother Dami's drowning and the failed rescue that ruined him. He snaps at Amara when she asks too many questions. The beat is grief surfacing like debris after a flood.

chapters.title: What the Cargo Holds
chapters.summary: POV Amara. A crate breaks open in rough water: inside are documents proving the gorge disaster was caused by a dam company's negligence — evidence that could clear Zephyrine but implicate the downstream village elders who took company money. The beat is moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Storm warnings force a choice: push upstream to deliver the evidence or shelter downstream near the village. Ines orders them forward; Zephyrine stalls, torn between duty to the contract and the people who once fed him. The beat is pressure without release.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: POV Amara. The Vela strikes submerged debris; the hull splits as the storm hits full force. Bailing side by side through the night, Amara and Zephyrine trade truths — her exile, his brother — and something unspoken settles between them. The beat is intimacy forged in emergency.

chapters.title: Ines's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Confronted mid-storm, Ines admits she needs the evidence not for justice but leverage against the company that ruined them both. Zephyrine realizes delivering it makes him her weapon. The beat is betrayal recognized too late, rage sharpened by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Head of the Gorge
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Climax: with the boat sinking, they beach at the head of the gorge. Zephyrine burns the evidence rather than let Ines weaponize it against the village, then hauls the crew through the flood to high ground, nearly losing Amara — and saving her. The beat is sacrifice as self-definition.

chapters.title: Where the River Ends
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Aftermath: Ines departs with nothing; the village shelters the wrecked crew anyway, asking no questions. Blacklisted still, Zephyrine chooses not to run — he'll rebuild the crossing route honestly, with Amara beside him. The beat is quiet arrival: stopping, at last, costing less than moving.
